description: Frontend sends one completed spiral drawing; backend returns a risk score plus per-feature breakdown against the UCI reference groups.

server.framework: FastAPI (Adam's branch). The frontend doesn't depend on the framework.
server.same_origin: Serve the frontend from the same server: GET / returns templates/index.html (plain HTML, no templating) and /static serves static/. The frontend calls the relative path /analyze; a different origin would need CORS plus a full URL in ANALYZE_ENDPOINT in app.js.
server.debug: Adam's existing HTML dashboard moves to /debug.

schema.x: float[] — CSS pixel X, canvas-relative (clientX minus canvas.getBoundingClientRect().left)
schema.y: float[] — CSS pixel Y, canvas-relative (clientY minus canvas.getBoundingClientRect().top)
schema.t: float[] — DOMHighResTimeStamp in ms, as captured from the PointerEvent (or its coalesced events); the S Pen reports roughly every 2ms
schema.p: float[] — S Pen pressure, 0.0-1.0, real values
schema.s: int[] — stroke ID: 0-based, +1 on every pen lift (pointerup or pointercancel). It is not a pen-down flag: every point sent is pen-down, hover samples are never recorded. Use the longest stroke (see preprocessing).
schema.canvas_width: float — CSS pixel width of the canvas the drawing was made on. Used only to scale x/y into UCI units before integer rounding (see preprocessing). Must be > 0: reject the request otherwise (a hidden canvas measures 0, which inflated coordinates ~580x and changed tremor).
schema.canvas_height: float — CSS pixel height of the canvas element. Same use as canvas_width.
schema.device_pixel_ratio: float — window.devicePixelRatio, typically 2.0 on Galaxy Tab S10 FE. Informational only; x/y are already CSS pixels, so the backend can ignore it.
schema.pointer_type: string — 'pen' or 'mouse'. Mouse pressure is a constant 0.5 (W3C spec), so pressure features are meaningless for 'mouse'. Tablet calibration applies only to 'pen'.
schema.num_strokes: int — computed as new Set(points.map(p => p.s)).size

spiral_template.direction: clockwise from the center, finishing at the top
spiral_template.why: Matches the UCI static spiral test (~2.7-2.9 turns drawn, clockwise). The deviation feature scores a perfectly drawn 2-turn spiral (0.030) worse than the average healthy UCI subject (0.028), so the original 2-turn template made healthy people look PD-like.

steps: Keep only the longest stroke (s value with the most points). UCI recordings are one continuous pass; joining strokes creates a fake jump at each pen lift.

Resample to an even 7ms grid with linear interpolation (UCI's rate). At the S Pen's ~2ms rate, integer coordinates move 0-1 unit per sample and that staircase inflates the tremor feature (measured: 0.111 at 2ms vs 0.084 at 7ms on the same drawing).

Convert to UCI line format X;Y;Z;Pressure;GripAngle;Timestamp;TestID (integers): scale x,y so the template spiral spans ~370 units, pressure * 1023, Z = 0, GripAngle = 0 (not available from PointerEvent, and unused by the features), timestamps in ms from 0, TestID = 0 (static spiral).
Run the existing feature extraction on that UCI-format data unchanged.
preprocessing.reference_implementation: 01/app.py — analyze() keeps the longest stroke; build_calibration() sets per-device factors from 01/calibration/<platform>/. 01/spiral_features.py — resample() puts the drawing on an even 100 Hz grid. The steps above describe the first prototype (since removed); the first 20 tablet drawings are in tablet_drawings/calibration/ (UCI format).

tablet_calibration.applies_to: pointer_type == 'pen' only. UCI reference data is never modified.

factors.tremor_pct: 1.0 (not calibrated — adding it changed nothing and the feature is noisy drawing to drawing)

tablet_calibration.how_derived: factor = UCI healthy mean / tablet healthy mean, from 20 healthy drawings on the Galaxy Tab S10 FE (4 people x 5, averaged per person first).
tablet_calibration.validation: Leave-one-person-out (each person's factor computed from the other three): healthy drawings scored >=50 went from 15/20 to 1/20. The remaining one was drawn at 13% pressure. Factor range across folds: p_cv 0.56-0.72, dev_norm 0.65-0.76. UCI leave-one-out accuracy is unchanged (13/15 healthy, 52/61 PD) because calibration only touches tablet input.
tablet_calibration.why_p_cv_differs: On both devices, lighter pressure means higher p_cv (correlation -0.71 tablet, -0.53 UCI healthy). UCI healthy subjects pressed at a median 84% of max; tablet users at 34-56%. At matched pressure (45-62%), tablet p_cv (0.157) is no higher than UCI healthy (0.181). The gap comes from people pressing more lightly on the tablet.
tablet_calibration.why_dev_norm_differs: Tablet deviation is ~1.4x UCI healthy even at steady pace and firm pressure; slower drawings ran somewhat higher (duration vs deviation correlation 0.32). Likely surface and display differences — the UCI data was recorded on a Wacom Cintiq 12WX pen display.
tablet_calibration.limitations: 4 healthy people only. No one with Parkinson's has drawn on this tablet, so it is assumed PD patients' values shift by the same factor. Recompute the factors if the device, template or preprocessing changes.
tablet_calibration.when_features_change: vel_cv has no tablet factor yet: once implemented, compare its tablet mean on the 20 calibration drawings with the UCI healthy mean, and add a factor only if it differs. After adding vel_cv and switching tremor to numpy + Hann, rerun both checks: UCI leave-one-out (currently 13/15 healthy, 52/61 PD) and the 20-drawing healthy check (currently 1/20 flagged leave-one-person-out).

input_checks.where: Frontend, before submitting (live drawings only; demo presets are exempt).
input_checks.why: UCI healthy subjects took 14-48 s. On the tablet, drawings under ~10 s or with very light pressure gave healthy people their highest scores; the 13%-pressure drawing scored 100 even after calibration. Failing drawings are redrawn rather than scored.

schema.level: int, 0-5, optional — Adam's existing level, kept alongside; the UI doesn't display it yet

<feature_key>.value: float — the patient's measured value, after tablet calibration
<feature_key>.ctrl_mean: float — mean of the healthy control reference group
<feature_key>.pd_mean: float — mean of the confirmed-PD reference group
<feature_key>.percentile_pd: int, 0-100 — position of value between the two means: (value - ctrl_mean) / (pd_mean - ctrl_mean) * 100, clamped to 0-100. 0 = at the healthy mean, 100 = at or past the PD mean. Not a percentile within either group. Direction is handled automatically: for dom_freq, where pd_mean < ctrl_mean, a lower value gives a higher number, so the UI needs no per-feature direction. The UI uses it only for the gauge pin and the card colour.
<feature_key>.scored: bool, optional, default true — false for display-only features (dom_freq); the UI tags those 'not in score'

schema.warnings: string[], optional — data-quality notes shown above the feature cards (short drawing, few samples, under one turn, mouse input)
schema.disclaimer: string — must be shown verbatim in the UI
schema.is_mock: bool, optional — true only from a mock backend; the UI shows a red MOCK DATA badge
schema.backend_label: string, optional — shown as a green badge for a real backend

dropped.p_norm: Mean of a self-normalized signal is always 1.0; raw pressure level is device-dependent.

feature_keys.status: dev_norm, p_cv, tremor_pct exist in Adam's branch today. vel_cv (scored; resampling + 9-point smoothing) and dom_freq (display-only; numpy FFT with a Hann window) are agreed but not yet implemented.

effect_sizes_cohens_d.tremor_pct: 0.78 (verified on all 15 controls; will change once tremor uses numpy + Hann — recompute)

example.interpretation: Example only — values shaped like a healthy tablet drawing after calibration.
example.disclaimer: Screening tool only. Not a clinical diagnosis. Please discuss any concerns with a clinician.

reference_dataset.source: UCI Parkinson Disease Spiral Drawings Using Digitized Graphics Tablet (dataset ID 395), recorded on a Wacom Cintiq 12WX at Istanbul University Cerrahpasa Faculty of Medicine
reference_dataset.groups: 15 healthy controls (all 15 usable — timestamps verified clean, no filtering) and 62 PD files (61 with static-spiral data: hw_dataset/parkinson + new_dataset/parkinson)
reference_dataset.filter: TestID == 0 (static spiral) only. 1 = dynamic spiral, 2 = circular motion.
reference_dataset.do_not: Do not drop controls to raise effect sizes: filtering to 7 controls inflates p_cv Cohen's d from 1.30 to 2.41.
